overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance data shows that high-velocity traction is concentrated in space and planetary 'What If' / extreme scenario formats published recently (late September/early October). Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' achieve exceptional views-per-day and engagement relative to older or purely abstract psychological facts. High-performing hooks leverage curiosity-driven counter-intuitive premises and scale comparisons.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on hypothetical falls into extreme planets (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y with 1029 views, 8KEl0_pJ_68 with 972 views) outperform standard passive fact statements by generating high view velocity within days of publishing.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more hypothetical planetary survival or immersive environment scenarios combined with staggering numerical facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre planetary laws (e.g., A9Qa-RmuOr0 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' with 981 views and 21 likes) drive strong engagement ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future space concepts on bizarre temporal, gravitational, or atmospheric laws of celestial bodies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older psychological fact shorts like Jc04LVKNd2s ('The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head') and 2fqaGqfsR4A ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') plateau rapidly with minimal likes and near-zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize abstract psychological trivia unless structured as an urgent, highly visual thriller micro-story.

weak_patterns.evidence: Static historical/archaeological questions (e.g., yLm-FjYH6-k) show slow lifetime accumulation without active viewer interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Shift historical content into dynamic, cinematic narrative storytelling or 'What If' alternate timelines.
